Subject: Incubex promo credits — conversion to Dedicated & packaging options

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking a look. Quick background: Incubex participated in the Startup Spark program in Sept and received $50k in promo credits. We're now shipping a customer-facing feature that calls the LLM heavily and the latency variability of the sandbox environment is becoming a blocker.

Two asks:
- Is there a way to convert some or all of our promo credits to a temporary Dedicated reservation (1–2 months) so we can guarantee throughput for launch?
- If conversion isn't possible, what packaging/discount exceptions do you offer for startups transitioning from promo credits to paid Dedicated capacity?

Our rough forecast for the first 30 days post-launch: ~60M tokens, peak concurrent throughput equivalent to 4 x A100-style instances. We don't yet have an enterprise contract; this would be a short-term bridge to a committed Dedicated plan.

Appreciate any flexibility and the steps you need from our side. Happy to jump on a short call — we're PST but can adjust.

Thanks,
Emma Torres
Head of Product
Incubex

Can you confirm the following so I can kick this to the pricing/ops team?
- Exact promo credit balance you have remaining (USD).
- Typical per-request token profile (avg input + output tokens).
- Target start date for launch and how long you need Dedicated throughput.

If you prefer, we can set a short call tomorrow to walk options — I can loop Ben (customer AE) and Laura (billing/finance) after I have the numbers. Attached is a short summary of our promo credits policy for reference.

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Emma — looping in Laura for billing nuance. Thanks for the forecast — that helps. Operationally there are three pragmatic paths we typically offer for startups in your situation: 

1) Short-term Dedicated conversion (provisional): convert up to X% of promo credits into a time-bound Dedicated reservation for 30–60 days. This requires an MSA addendum and a provisional invoice to track the reserved capacity. There's usually a modest uplift (we account for reserved slots).

2) Hybrid bridge: leave promo credits on the hosted account for baseline traffic and buy a small Dedicated pool for peak/bursty workload. This reduces total credits consumed and can be cheaper if your baseline is low.

3) Extended sandbox + priority routing: keep credits as-is and purchase a short-term priority routing add-on to reduce variance without full Dedicated.

What we need from you to run a quick pro forma: remaining promo credit USD amount, the monthly token estimate (you mentioned 60M), and a target launch date. If you're comfortable sharing a usage sample, that speeds kernel sizing (we can also vendor-run a short spike test).

Diego — filing the above as a straw proposal. Laura, do we have precedent for converting promo credits to a provisional reservation (30–60d) without a full committed contract?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Signed MSA + a 45-day addendum to track the provisional reservation and accounting treatment (DocuSign link below).
- A provisional invoice (zero-due balance until conversion triggers billing adjustments) to be issued before Nov 18 so we can allocate capacity.
- No permanent change to the promo credit expiry unless you later convert to a committed Dedicated contract.

I'll put a draft addendum into DocuSign now; signing will start the allocation queue. If you need the hybrid option instead, we can size a small Dedicated pool for peaks and keep the rest of the credits on hosted.
